arxiv-1906-09865.title: The Minimum Tollbooth Problem in Atomic Network Congestion Games with Unsplittable Flows
arxiv-1906-09865.creator: Julian Nickerl
arxiv-1906-09865.description: Abstract This work analyzes the minimum tollbooth problem in atomic network congestion games with unsplittable flows. The goal is to place tolls on edges, such that there exists a pure Nash equilibrium in the tolled game that is a social optimum in the untolled one. Additionally, we require the number of tolled edges to be the minimum.

arxiv-2111-04140.title: The Main Sequence of quasars: the taming of the extremes Publication type: Review Thanks: Invited talk presented at the X iii Serbian Meeting on spectral line shapes in astrophysics (SCSLSA)
arxiv-2111-04140.creator: P. Marziani*, E. Bon, N. Bon, M. D’Onofrio, B. Punsly, M. Śniegowska, B. Czerny, S. Panda, M. L. Martínez Aldama, A. del Olmo, A. Deconto-Machado, C. A. Negrete, D. Dultzin, T. Buendia, K. Garnica
arxiv-2111-04140.description: Abstract The last few years have seen the confirmation of several trends associated with the quasar main sequence. The idea of a main sequence for quasars is relatively recent, and its full potential for the observational classification and contextualization of quasars’ properties has yet to be fully exploited.

arxiv-2112-05171.title: Quantum Hair and Black Hole Information
arxiv-2112-05171.creator: Xavier Calmet, Stephen D. H. Hsu
arxiv-2112-05171.description: Abstract It has been shown that the quantum state of the graviton field outside a black hole horizon carries information about the internal state of the hole. We explain how this allows unitary evaporation: the final radiation state is a complex superposition which depends linearly on the initial black hole state.

arxiv-2206-02754.title: Warm ionized gas in the blue compact galaxy Haro 14 viewed by MUSE Thanks: Based on observations made with ESO Telescopes at Paranal Observatory under programme ID 60.A-9186(A)
arxiv-2206-02754.creator: L. M. Cairós, J.N. González-Pérez, P. M. Weilbacher, R. Manso Sainz
arxiv-2206-02754.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by L. M. Cairós, J.N. González-Pérez, P. M. Weilbacher, R. Manso Sainz. We investigate the warm ionized gas in the blue compact galaxy (BCG) Haro 14 by means of integral field spectroscopic observations taken with the Multi Unit Spectroscopic Explorer (MUSE) at the Very Large Telescope. The large field of view of MUSE and its unprecedented sensitivity enable observations of the galaxy nebular emission up to large galactocentric distances, even in the important but very faint [O i ] λ \lambda 6300 diagnostic line.

arxiv-2303-16078.title: Practical solutions to the relative pose of three calibrated cameras
arxiv-2303-16078.creator: Charalambos Tzamos, Viktor Kocur, Yaqing Ding 1 {1}, Daniel Barath 3 {3}, Zuzana Berger Haladová 2 {2}, Torsten Sattler 4 {4}, Zuzana Kukelova 1 {1}
arxiv-2303-16078.description: Abstract We study the challenging problem of estimating the relative pose of three calibrated cameras from four point correspondences. We propose novel efficient solutions to this problem that are based on the simple idea of using four correspondences to estimate an approximate geometry of the first two views.

arxiv-2401-05985.title: Axially Symmetric Quadrupole-Octupole Model incorporating Sextic Potential
arxiv-2401-05985.creator: M. Chabab, A. El Batoul, L. El Ouaourti
arxiv-2401-05985.description: Abstract We present an extended application of the analytic quadrupole octupole axially symmetric model, originally employed to study the octupole deformation and vibrations in light actinides using an infinite well potential (IW). In this work, we extend the model’s applicability to a broader range of nuclei exhibiting octupole deformation by incorporating a sextic potential instead of the Davidson potential.

arxiv-2507-15338.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Takaho Shimokasa, Hiroyuki Yomo, Federico Chiariotti, Junya Shiraishi, Petar Popovski. This paper investigates how to achieve both low-power operations of sensor nodes and accurate state estimation using Kalman filter for internet of things (IoT) monitoring employing wireless sensor networks under radio resource constraint.

arxiv-2507-22509.title: A quasi-optimal upper bound for induced paths in sparse graphs
arxiv-2507-22509.creator: Basile Couëtoux, Oscar Defrain, Jean-Florent Raymond
arxiv-2507-22509.description: Abstract In 2012, Nešetřil and Ossona de Mendez proved that graphs of bounded degeneracy that have a path of order n n also have an induced path of order Ω ⁡ ( log ⁡ log ⁡ n ) \Omega(\log\log n) .

arxiv-2512-04730.title: On the magnetic field evolution of interplanetary coronal mass ejections from 0.07 to 5.4 au
arxiv-2512-04730.creator: Christian Möstl, Emma E. Davies, Eva Weiler, Hannah T. Rüdisser, Ute V. Amerstorfer, Andreas J. Weiss, Martin A. Reiss, Satabdwa Majumdar, Timothy S. Horbury, Stuart D. Bale, Daniel Heyner
arxiv-2512-04730.description: Abstract A central question for understanding interplanetary coronal mass ejection (ICME) physics and improving space weather forecasting is how ICMEs evolve in interplanetary space. We have updated one of the most comprehensive in situ ICME catalogs to date, which now includes 1976 events from 11 space missions covering over 34 years, from December 1990 to August 2025.

pmc-11328602.title: Pain, function and peritendinous effusion improvement after dry needling in patients with long head of biceps brachii tendinopathy: a single-blind randomized clinical trial
pmc-11328602.creator: I-Wei Chen, Ying-Tzu Liao, Hsin Tseng, Hsiao-Che Lin, Li-Wei Chou
pmc-11328602.description: IntroductionLong head of biceps brachii tendinopathy, a frequent source of anterior shoulder pain, may lead to discomfort and diminished function. The objective of this study is to assess the efficacy of dry needling and transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation in these patients.

pmc-11464113.title: Benefit delayed immunosenescence by regulating CD4 +T cells: A promising therapeutic target for aging‐related diseases
pmc-11464113.creator: Tingting Xia, Ying Zhou, Jiayao An, Zhi Cui, Xinqin Zhong, Tianyi Cui, Bin Lv, Xin Zhao, Xiumei Gao
pmc-11464113.description: CD4+T cells play a notable role in immune protection at different stages of life. During aging, the interaction between the body's internal and external environment and CD4+T cells results in a series of changes in the CD4+T cells pool making it involved in immunosenescence.

pmc-11518834.title: The impact of confirmation bias awareness on mitigating susceptibility to misinformation
pmc-11518834.creator: Michal Piksa, Karolina Noworyta, Aleksander Gundersen, Jonas Kunst, Mikolaj Morzy, Jan Piasecki, Rafal Rygula
pmc-11518834.description: IntroductionIn the current digital age, the proliferation of misinformation presents a formidable challenge to a democratic society. False narratives surrounding vaccination efforts pose a significant public health risk. Understanding the role of cognitive biases in susceptibility to misinformation is crucial in addressing this challenge.

pmc-11696604.title: The role of empiric atypical antibiotic coverage in non-severe community-acquired pneumonia
pmc-11696604.creator: Whitney Hartlage, Hannah Imlay, Emily S Spivak
pmc-11696604.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). A β–lactam plus a macrolide or a respiratory fluoroquinolone alone is recommended as standard empiric antibacterial therapy for non-severe adults hospitalized with community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) per Infectious Diseases Society of America guidelines. However, the evidence in support of adding empiric atypical antibacterial therapy, and specifically the addition of a macrolide, is conflicting and should be balanced with additional factors: the necessity of covering atypical organisms, benefits of macrolide-associated immunomodulation, harms associated with antibiotic use, and selection for antibiotic-resistant organisms.

pmc-12999539.creator: Saritha Shamsunder, Leela Digumarti, Bhagyalaxmi Nayak, Vasantha Dasari, Archana Mishra, Anita Kumar, Sony Nanda, Jugal Kishore, Nishi Choudhary

pmc-13156580.title: Calcified cerebral emboli—A case series
pmc-13156580.creator: Anmol Kakaria, Yannick Yangue
pmc-13156580.description: Calcified Cerebral Emboli (CCE) was first reported in 1981 and is an increasingly common yet under-reported cause of acute ischemic stroke (AIS). We present 2 rare cases of acute ischemic stroke due to calcified cerebral emboli. Calcified cerebral emboli are identified on CT scan of the brain with a follow-up MRI to show area of ischemia.

pmc-13233478.title: Assessing patterns, barriers, and motivations for family planning utilization among currently pregnant women in Nigeria: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13233478.creator: Ayodamola Bakare, Kofoworola Akinsola, Julius Salako, Olabisi Olasupo, Carina King, Adegoke G. Falade, Ayobami A. Bakare
pmc-13233478.description: IntroductionUniversal access to family planning is critical to reducing maternal mortality, yet progress remains slow, particularly in Sub-Saharan Africa. In Nigeria, modern contraceptive use is 12%, compared to a global average of 77.5%. This study, therefore assessed contraceptive use patterns, barriers, and motivations among pregnant women to inform the design of context-specific interventions aimed at improving family planning uptake.

pmc-13457782.title: Effect of endoscopic submucosal dissection on short-term surgical outcome after radical gastrectomy: a multicenter retrospective study based on the Korean Gastric Cancer Association nationwide survey
pmc-13457782.creator: Jinjoo Kim, Ki Bum Park, Han Hong Lee
pmc-13457782.description: PurposeEndoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) is a minimally invasive treatment for early gastric cancer (EGC) with a low risk of lymph node metastasis. However, 17%–21% of patients require additional curative gastrectomy (ACG) due to non-curative factors. Although ESD may induce fibrosis or adhesions that could complicate subsequent surgery, its impact on surgical outcomes after ACG remains unclear.

pmc-13629154.title: Auditory Brainstem Encoding of Speech-in-Noise Predicts Word Identification, Narrative Comprehension, and Subjective Listening Effort in a Selective Attention Task
pmc-13629154.creator: Kelsey Mankel, Daniel C. Comstock, Brett M. Bormann, Soukhin Das, Doron Sagiv, Hilary Brodie, Lee M. Miller
pmc-13629154.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The auditory brainstem plays a crucial role in speech-in-noise (SiN) listening, refining numerous acoustic features such as pitch and spatial location under continual descending influence from the cortex. However, the difficulty of characterizing brainstem activity during continuous speech listening has obscured its functional role in ecologically valid contexts—not only the effects of selective attention on neural responses but also their impact on comprehension and listening effort.
